subject.title: [Feature]: openclaw notify — admin-scoped push to connected UI sessions

question: Should OpenClaw core expose a shell-facing admin notification broadcast to connected Control UI sessions, and what auth scope, payload, targeting, delivery, and abuse-control contract should it use?
rationale: Current main lacks the requested surface, but adding it creates a new core CLI/Gateway/UI API and security boundary that automation should not choose by implication.

options.title: Define a narrow core notify contract
options.body: Add an explicit admin-scoped CLI/Gateway/Control UI notification path with sanitized payloads, targeting semantics, abuse controls, docs, and focused tests.

options.title: Fold into broader WebUI notification architecture
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/20237 explicitly own the shell/admin Gateway API before this narrower request is closed or implemented.

options.title: Defer outside core
options.body: Leave shell alerts to plugins/hooks or future plugin API work until maintainers decide core should own connected-UI notifications.

recommendation.title: Define a narrow core notify contract
recommendation.body: Add an explicit admin-scoped CLI/Gateway/Control UI notification path with sanitized payloads, targeting semantics, abuse controls, docs, and focused tests.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice spans the current core CLI, Gateway event authorization, and product/security boundaries that recent history ties most strongly to steipete.
